The sea is before us; if we cross it we drown, and Pharaoh is behind us; if he catches us, we are killed.' ﴿We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.﴾

Then Moses said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you act﴾, and he said: ﴿No indeed! My Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾. Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾, and he struck it, but it did not split. He said: "I am more forward than you and stronger in creation." Allah the Exalted then revealed to Moses: "Be quiet, and say: 'Split, O Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.'" He did so, and the sea split and became twelve paths, one for each tribe. Allah uncovered the face of the earth, and it became dry, and between every two paths a mountain rose.

They were cousins who could not see one another or hear one another's speech, so each group said: "Our companions have drowned." Allah the Exalted revealed to the mountains in the water: "Be interlaced," and they interlaced and became like openings in it, so that they could see one another.

When Pharaoh arrived with his armies at the sea and saw the sea in that state, Pharaoh said: "The sea has frightened me," and they feared entering the sea. Pharaoh was on a black stallion, and there was no mare among Pharaoh's horses. Gabriel came on a mare in heat [wadiq: one that desires the stallion], entered the sea, and Michael drove them, so no man strayed from them without his being joined to them.

When Pharaoh's black stallion smelled the scent of Gabriel's mare, and Pharaoh could not see it, it slipped after Gabriel's mare, and Pharaoh had no control over his affair at all. The horses plunged into the water, and when the last of them entered the sea and the first wished to come out, the water closed over them. When Pharaoh faced drowning he said: ﴿I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims﴾. Gabriel said: ﴿Now? And you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.﴾

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Allah said to Moses and Harun: ﴿Speak to him gently, that perhaps he may remember or fear﴾, when his remembrance and fear would no longer benefit him.

Ka'b said: When the Nile of Egypt stopped flowing, the Copts said to Pharaoh: "If you are our lord, make the water flow for us." He mounted and ordered his troops to mount. His herald would call every hour: "Let so-and-so stand with his troops, commander by commander." They stood upon their ranks until only he and his close attendants remained. He ordered them to stand, until only his chamberlains and servants remained; he ordered them to stand, and advanced alone, out of their sight, [and dismounted from his mount], and put on other garments, prostrated, and humbled himself before Allah. Allah made the water flow for him. Then Gabriel came to him alone in the form of a questioner and said: "What does the commander say about a man who has a slave who grew up in his blessings, having no master but him, who then denied his blessings, rejected his right, and claimed sovereignty over him?" [Pharaoh wrote: "His recompense is that he be drowned in the sea."] [[addition from al-Qurtubi's tafsir.]]

When Moses informed his people of the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, the Children of Israel said: "Pharaoh did not die and will never die." So Allah commanded the sea, and it threw Pharaoh onto the shore, a red, short creature like a bull. The Children of Israel saw him, and then the sea [they crossed it]. Al-Hasan read "wa-jawwaznā" (both are dialects of the same meaning).

﴿So Pharaoh pursued them﴾, that is, caught up with them. It is said: "tabi'ahu" and "atba'ahu" when one catches up with and overtakes someone, while "ittaba'ahu" with doubled ta' means he went behind him [and imitated him]. ﴿Pharaoh and his armies.﴾

﴿Out of insolence and enmity﴾: zulm (injustice) and transgression. It is said: 'ada ya'dū 'adwan, like ghazā yaghzū ghazwan. Al-Hasan read ('udūwan) with a damma on the ayn and shadda on the waw, like 'alā ya'lū 'ulūwan. The exegetes said: "bagyan" refers to speech and "'adwan" to action.

﴿Until, when drowning overtook him﴾, meaning it encompassed him. ﴿He said: "I believe that..."﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "innahu" with a kasra, meaning "I believe, and I said: 'indeed'," and this is the reading of Abdullah. The others read "annahu" with a fatha, because "āmantu" governs it; this is the preference of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

﴿There is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.﴾ Gabriel said: ﴿Now? And you disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters.﴾

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gabriel said to me: 'I have never hated any of Allah's servants except that I hated two servants: one of the jinn and the other of mankind. As for the one of the jinn, it is Iblis when he refused to prostrate to Adam; as for the one of mankind, it is Pharaoh when he said: ﴿I am your highest lord﴾. And if you had seen me, O Muhammad, putting the mud into his mouth, for fear that mercy would reach him.'" [86] [[al-Tabari's Jami' al-Bayan: 19/102, with slight variation.]]

﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾, meaning We will place you on a raised place of the earth, and this is the najw, the high place. Aws ibn Hajar said:
"He who is in his high place is like one who is in his najwah,
and the one who hides is like one who walks in the open."

﴿In your body﴾: in your flesh without spirit in you. Mujahid and al-Kisa'i said: "Badan" here means armour, and he was wearing armour. Al-A'sha said:
"A fair one like a bright stream, woven, with a helmet above the front of the coat of mail."

Abdullah read: ﴿So today We will save you in your body﴾, meaning We will cast you upon the shore of the sea. It was also said: "your hair."

﴿That you may be a sign for those after you﴾: a lesson and admonition.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) read: "li-man khalaqaka" with a qaf, meaning: that you may be a sign for your Creator.

﴿And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs.﴾ Muqatil said: this means the people of Mecca. Al-Hasan said: it is general.

﴿Of Our signs﴾, that is, concerning faith in Our signs, [they are] heedless.

﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (We settled the Children of Israel in a good dwelling), meaning: We made them descend (أنزلنا) into a good abode after the destruction of Pharaoh. It is said: "a good abode" means something excellent. It is also said that it refers to al-Urdunn (Jordan) and Filastin (Palestine), which is the Holy Land that Allah blessed for Ibrahim and his descendants. Al-Dahhak said: it is Egypt and al-Sham (Greater Syria).

﴿وَرَزَقْنَاهُم مِّنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ (and We provided them with good things): the lawful things.

﴿فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ (Then they did not differ): meaning the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿حَتَّى جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ﴾ (until knowledge came to them): the clear evidence that Muhammad (ﷺ) speaks the truth and that his religion is true. It is also said that ʿilm here means the known thing (al-maʿlum), according to their saying of the created: "khalq" (created), and of the decreed: "qadar." Here the text breaks off: [....... فتم طرف الأمر، قال الله.....] [[So it is in the original.]]. The meaning of the verse is: they did not differ concerning Muhammad until the known thing came to them, which is that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a prophet, because they used to know him before he came forth.

﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ (Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ): concerning the religion.

﴿فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّا أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ (So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you), the verse. The scholars have said much in explaining the meaning of this verse. Muqatil said: the disbelievers of Makkah said, "This revelation is only cast upon the tongue of Muhammad by a devil." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed:

﴿فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّا أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ means: the Qur'an.

﴿فَاسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ (then ask those who read the Book before you): they will inform you that it is written in their Torah: a messenger, a prophet.

It is also said: the address is to the Messenger (ﷺ), but what is meant is others among those who doubt him, as the Arabs have a custom of addressing a man with a thing while meaning someone else. Like the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ (O Prophet, fear Allah). It is as if the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) while what is meant is the believers. This is shown by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted), where it says "ta'maluna" (you do) and not "ta'malu" (he does).

The exegetes said: the people in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "We believe in Allah," with their tongues, and among them was a disbelieving denier who does not see except that what he brought is false, or a doubter in the matter who does not know what it is, putting one foot forward and another back. So Allah addressed this category of people and said: ﴿فَإِنْ كُنْتَ﴾ (So if you are), O human, ﴿فِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّا أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ (in doubt about what We have sent down to you), of guidance, upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿فَاسْأَلِ الأَكَابِرَ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ (then ask the elders among the scholars of the People of the Book), such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, Salman al-Farisi, Tamim al-Dari and those like them, so they may testify to his truthfulness. He did not mean the stubborn ones among them.

It is also said: inna (إن) here means ma (ما), and its estimate is: "So I was not in doubt about what We sent down to you; so ask, O people, you, not the Prophet." As He said: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ﴾ (though their plotting was such that the mountains would be moved by it), meaning: "and their plotting was not..."

It is also said: Allah knew that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not doubt, but He wished to make the Messenger take up the words "I do not doubt and I do not dispute" as a continuation of the proof against the doubters among his people. Just as He says to ʿIsa: ﴿أَأَنتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"), while He knows that he did not say it, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾ (Exalted are You; it is not for me to say what I have no right to), a continuation of the proof against the Christians.

Al-Farra' said: Allah, exalted is He, knew that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not doubting, so He said to him: ﴿فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ﴾, and this is like when you say to your slave, of whose lordship you have no doubt: "If you are my slave, obey me," or you say to your son: "If you are my son, be dutiful to me."

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: the one who doubts a thing is constrained in his chest, so a person of constrained chest is called "shakk" (doubting). He says: "If you are straitened by what you witness of their obstinacy and harm, then be patient, and ask those who read the Book before you, and they will tell you how the Prophets were patient with the harm of their people, and how the outcome of their affair was victory and establishment."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qattan say concerning this: it was permissible for the Messenger (ﷺ) to have the whisperings of Satan, because striving against them earns great reward, and Allah [.........] [[unreadable words in the manuscript]]; and his chest was constrained by that. And Allah knows best. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: with [the conditional particle] [[so it is in the original]], the condition does not establish the act.

The evidence for this is what was narrated: when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I do not doubt and I do not ask." [87] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/317, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/218.]]

Then He gave a ruling [and provided] [[so it is in the original]] with speech, saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكَ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ (The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters), ﴿وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (and do not be among those who denied the signs of Allah), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ (and thus be among the losers) [whose deeds are nullified].

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ (Indeed those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified): His curse upon them [for their hypocrisy]. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "wrath will descend upon you." And he said: Allah created the creation, [so among them is the wretched and among them] the blessed. Whoever is blessed does not disbelieve except briefly before he returns to faith, and whoever is wretched does not believe except briefly before he returns to disbelief; and the deeds are only [ ... ] [[a blank in the original]]. The people of Madina read "kalimat" (words) in the plural.

﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ * وَلَوْ جَاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ﴾ (They will not believe, even if every sign should come to them), meaning proof, ﴿حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ﴾ (until they see the painful punishment). Al-Akhfash said: he made the verb "kull" (every) feminine because it is attached to a feminine noun, and the word "kull" is the same for masculine and feminine.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qattan say concerning this: it was permissible for the Messenger (ﷺ) to have the whisperings of Satan, because striving against them earns great reward, and Allah [.........] [[unreadable words in the manuscript]]; and his chest was constrained by that. And Allah knows best. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: with [the conditional particle] [[so it is in the original]], the condition does not establish the act.

The evidence for this is what was narrated: when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I do not doubt and I do not ask." [87] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/317, and Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 11/218.]]

Then He gave a ruling [and provided] [[so it is in the original]] with speech, saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكَ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ (The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters), ﴿وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (and do not be among those who denied the signs of Allah), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ (and thus be among the losers) [whose deeds are nullified].

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ﴾ (Indeed those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified): His curse upon them [for their hypocrisy]. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "wrath will descend upon you." And he said: Allah created the creation, [so among them is the wretched and among them] the blessed. Whoever is blessed does not disbelieve except briefly before he returns to faith, and whoever is wretched does not believe except briefly before he returns to disbelief; and the deeds are only [ ... ] [[a blank in the original]]. The people of Madina read "kalimat" (words) in the plural.

﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ * وَلَوْ جَاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ﴾ (They will not believe, even if every sign should come to them), meaning proof, ﴿حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ﴾ (until they see the painful punishment). Al-Akhfash said: he made the verb "kull" (every) feminine because it is attached to a feminine noun, and the word "kull" is the same for masculine and feminine.

So-why-not (﴿فَلَوْلا﴾) means فهلّا (fa-hallā, "why was it not that..."). It is likewise so in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy. The poet says:

You count the slaughter of she-camels your greatest glory, [O sons of Dawtari], were it not for the armored horsemen.

That is, فهلّا.

﴿آمَنَتْ﴾ ("believed") at the moment of seeing the punishment, ﴿فَنَفَعَها إِيمانُها﴾ ("so its belief benefited it") at the time of despair, ﴿إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾ ("except the people of Yunus"). The meaning is: "But the people of Yunus..." as in the words of al-Nābigha:

I stood there at dusk, asking it,
it failed to answer; and there was no one in the abode.

wa-l-nuʾyu ka-l-ḥawḍi bi-l-maẓlūmati l-jalad.

(al-Awārī: singular ārin, a rope with which a beast is tied. Al-Laʾy: hardship. Al-Nuʾy: a trench around the tent that keeps water from reaching it. Al-Jalad: hard ground. The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari, 1/117.)

﴿لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمْ عَذابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَمَتَّعْناهُمْ إِلى حِينٍ﴾ ("When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy for a time"), that is, until the time their terms ended. Some said: their belief benefited them at the time of despair because a portion of their terms remained, so they were saved for what remained of their terms. As for the belief of one whose term has ended, it does not benefit him at the presence of punishment.

The story of the verse, as related by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Suddī, Wahb and others, is that the people of Yunus were at Nineveh, in the land of Mosul. God sent Yunus to call them to Islam and to leave what they were upon. He called them, but they refused. It was said to him: "Tell them that the punishment will come to them within three [days]." He told them, and they said:

"We have never tried him in a lie. So wait: if he stays among you that night, then he is nothing. And if he does not stay, know that the punishment will reach you in the morning." When it was the middle of the night, he went out on foot from among them. When they awoke in the morning, the punishment enveloped them as a short garment envelops its wearer when he enters it.

Muqatil said: the punishment was above their heads by a distance of one mile. Ibn ʿAbbas said: a distance of two-thirds of a mile. Wahb said: the sky became clouded with a black, terrifying cloud which brought a severe smoke. It descended until it covered their city, and their rooftops turned black. When they saw that, they became certain of destruction and sought their prophet, but did not find him. God cast repentance into their hearts. They went out to the open ground, themselves, their women, their children and their animals, wore wool garments, showed belief and repentance, and made their intention sincere. They separated every mother from her child, among the people and the livestock, so some yearned for others. Their voices rose and mixed with the voices of their animals, and the animals' cries mixed with theirs. They cried out and wailed to God Most High and said: "We believe in what Yunus brought." Their Lord had mercy on them, answered their supplication, and removed the punishment from them after it had overshadowed them and descended within earshot. That was the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.

Ibn Masʿūd said: the repentance of the people of Nineveh reached the point that they returned the wrongs among themselves, so that a man would come to a stone on which a foundation had been laid, pull it up and return it.

Ṣāliḥ al-Murri related from Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī, from Abū al-Jald, who said: When the punishment covered the people of Yunus, they went to a shaykh from among the remnants of their scholars and said to him: "The punishment has descended upon us, so what do you think?" He said: "Say:

Yā ḥayy ḥīna lā ḥayy, wa-yā ḥayy, [yā] muḥyi l-mawtā, wa-yā ḥayy, lā ilāha illā anta."

They said it, the punishment was removed from them, and they were allowed to enjoy for a time.

They said: Yunus (peace be upon him) had promised them the punishment, so he went out waiting for the punishment and the destruction of his people, but he saw nothing. Whoever lied and had no proof was killed. So Yunus, when the punishment was removed from them, said: "How can I return to my people after I have called them liars?" He set off angry at his Lord, displeased with his people, and came to the sea, where there was a ship loaded [and he boarded it] alone without a fare. When he entered it, the ship stopped, while the other ships were sailing right and left. They said:

"What is wrong with your ship?" Yunus said: "There is a runaway slave in it, and it will not move until you cast him out." They said: "You are the prophet, so we will not cast you out." They drew lots, and the lot fell on him three times, so he fell into the water, and a fish was appointed to swallow him.

Ibn Masʿūd said: the fish swallowed him and went with him until it reached the bottom of the earth. He remained in its belly for forty nights, and he heard the glorifying of the pebbles. Then he called out in the darkness: ﴿أَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ ("There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers"). God answered him, commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore of the sea [naked]. God caused a gourd plant to grow over him, and he began to shade himself under it. God appointed a young goat to him, which drank from its milk. Then the plant withered, and he wept over it. God revealed to him: "You weep over a plant that withered, but you do not weep over one hundred thousand people whom I destroyed!" Yunus went out and found a boy herding. He said: "Who are you, boy?"

The boy said: "From the people of Yunus." He said: "When you return to them, tell them that you met Yunus." The boy said: "If you are Yunus, you know that I have no proof. [If] I say so, who will testify for me?" Yunus said: "This land and this tree will testify for you." The boy said: "Let me see them." Yunus said: "When this boy comes to you, testify for him." They said: "Yes." The boy returned to his people and said to the king: "I have met Yunus, and he sends you greetings." The boy had brothers and was in a position of strength, so the king ordered his execution. He said: "I have proof." They slipped away with him to the land and the tree. The boy said: "I beseech you both: did Yunus bear witness for me?" They said: "Yes." The people returned in fear and said to the king:

"The tree and the land have borne witness for him." The king took the boy's hand, seated him in his own place, and said: "You are more entitled to this place than I am." Ibn Masʿūd said: he then appointed the boy as their ruler among them for forty years.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "He would have compelled them to belief." Al-Akhfash said: He brought "jamīʿan" with "kulluhum" as emphasis, like His saying ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ ("Do not take two gods").

Ibn ʿAbbas said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was eager that all people should believe and pledge allegiance to him upon guidance. God informed him that none believes except one for whom God has already decreed happiness in the earlier Book, and none goes astray except one for whom God has already decreed wretchedness in the earlier Remembrance.

﴿وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ﴾ ("And it is not for any soul") — al-Ḥasan said: "It is not fitting for any soul." Al-Mubarrad said: its meaning is: "You could not believe except by God's permission," ﴿إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "by God's command." ʿAṭāʾ said: "by God's will," like His saying ﴿وَما هُمْ بِضارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("They could not harm anyone by it except by God's permission"). Al-Kūfī said: "what has preceded of His decree." Al-[Dānī] said: "by His knowledge and His enabling."

﴿وَيَجْعَلُ﴾ ("And He places"), that is, "and God places." al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim read it with the nūn (﴿وَنَجْعَلُ﴾, "and We place"). ﴿الرِّجْسَ﴾ ("the abomination") means the punishment and wrath. al-Aʿmash read ﴿الرجز﴾ with a zāy, ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ("upon those who do not reason") — the proofs of God regarding monotheism and prophethood.

﴿قُلِ﴾ ("Say") — O Muhammad — to these polytheists who ask you for signs: ﴿انْظُرُوا ماذا فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ ("Look at what is in the heavens"), namely the sun, moon and stars, ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ ("and the earth"), namely the mountains, seas, rivers, trees and other signs. Then He said: ﴿وَما تُغْنِي الْآياتُ وَالنُّذُرُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe"), in the knowledge of God.

﴿فَهَلْ يَنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ ("So do they await") — that is, the polytheists of Mecca — ﴿إِلَّا مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾ ("except the like of the days of those who passed away"), that is, passed on ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ ("before them"), from those who passed away. Qatada said: it means the encounters of God with the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd. The Arabs call punishment and blessing "days," like His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("And remind them of the days of God"). Everything that has passed over you of good or evil is "days."

﴿قُلْ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ﴾ ("Say: Wait, I am with you among those who wait").

﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("Then We save Our messengers and those who believed") with them when the punishment descends. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ ("Thus") — as We saved them.

﴿كَذلِكَ حَقًّا﴾ ("Thus, as a truth") — obligatory — ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ ("upon Us"), without doubt, ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("We save the believers") through you, O Muhammad. Yaʿqūb read ﴿نُنْجِ رُسُلَنا﴾ with lightening (the single nūn), and al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ with lightening, while the others doubled them. Wahb said: the sky became clouded with a black, terrifying cloud which brought a severe smoke. It descended until it covered their city, and their rooftops turned black. They separated every mother from her child, among the people and the livestock, so some yearned for others. Ibn Masʿūd said: the repentance of the people of Nineveh reached the point that they returned the wrongs among themselves, so that a man would come to a stone on which a foundation had been laid, pull it up and return it.

They said it, the punishment was removed from them, and they were allowed to enjoy for a time.

They said: Yunus (peace be upon him) had promised them the punishment, so he went out waiting for the punishment and the destruction of his people, but he saw nothing. Whoever lied and had no proof was killed. So Yunus, when the punishment was removed from them, said: "How can I return to my people after I have called them liars?" He set off angry at his Lord, displeased with his people, and came to the sea, where there was a ship loaded [and he boarded it] alone without a fare. When he entered it, the ship stopped, while the other ships were sailing right and left. They said:

"What is wrong with your ship?" Yunus said: "There is a runaway slave in it, and it will not move until you cast him out." They said: "You are the prophet, so we will not cast you out." God answered him, commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore of the sea [naked]. God caused a gourd plant to grow over him, and he began to shade himself under it. God appointed a young goat to him, which drank from its milk. Then the plant withered, and he wept over it. God revealed to him: "You weep over a plant that withered, but you do not weep over one hundred thousand people whom I destroyed!" Yunus went out and found a boy herding. He said: "Who are you, boy?"

The boy said: "From the people of Yunus." He said: "When you return to them, tell them that you met Yunus." The boy said: "If you are Yunus, you know that I have no proof. [If] I say so, who will testify for me?" Yunus said: "This land and this tree will testify for you." The boy said: "Let me see them." Yunus said: "When this boy comes to you, testify for him." They said: "Yes." The boy returned to his people and said to the king: "I have met Yunus, and he sends you greetings." The boy had brothers and was in a position of strength, so the king ordered his execution. He said: "I have proof." They slipped away with him to the land and the tree. The boy said: "I beseech you both: did Yunus bear witness for me?" They said: "Yes." The people returned in fear and said to the king:

"The tree and the land have borne witness for him." The king took the boy's hand, seated him in his own place, and said: "You are more entitled to this place than I am." Ibn Masʿūd said: he then appointed the boy as their ruler among them for forty years.

﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ ("And if your Lord had willed") — O Muhammad — ﴿لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾ ("all those on earth would have believed, all of them together"). Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: "He would have compelled them to belief." Al-Akhfash said: He brought "jamīʿan" with "kulluhum" as emphasis, like His saying ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ ("Do not take two gods").

﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("Would you then compel the people until they become believers?")

Ibn ʿAbbas said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was eager that all people should believe and pledge allegiance to him upon guidance. God informed him that none believes except one for whom God has already decreed happiness in the earlier Book, and none goes astray except one for whom God has already decreed wretchedness in the earlier Remembrance.

﴿وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ﴾ ("And it is not for any soul") — al-Ḥasan said: "It is not fitting for any soul." Al-Mubarrad said: its meaning is: "You could not believe except by God's permission," ﴿إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "by God's command." ʿAṭāʾ said: "by God's will," like His saying ﴿وَما هُمْ بِضارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("They could not harm anyone by it except by God's permission"). Al-Kūfī said: "what has preceded of His decree." Al-[Dānī] said: "by His knowledge and His enabling."

﴿وَيَجْعَلُ﴾ ("And He places"), that is, "and God places." al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim read it with the nūn (﴿وَنَجْعَلُ﴾, "and We place"). ﴿الرِّجْسَ﴾ ("the abomination") means the punishment and wrath. al-Aʿmash read ﴿الرجز﴾ with a zāy, ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ ("upon those who do not reason") — the proofs of God regarding monotheism and prophethood.

﴿قُلِ﴾ ("Say") — O Muhammad — to these polytheists who ask you for signs: ﴿انْظُرُوا ماذا فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ ("Look at what is in the heavens"), namely the sun, moon and stars, ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ ("and the earth"), namely the mountains, seas, rivers, trees and other signs. Then He said: ﴿وَما تُغْنِي الْآياتُ وَالنُّذُرُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe"), in the knowledge of God.

﴿فَهَلْ يَنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ ("So do they await") — that is, the polytheists of Mecca — ﴿إِلَّا مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾ ("except the like of the days of those who passed away"), that is, passed on ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ ("before them"), from those who passed away. Qatada said: it means the encounters of God with the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd. The Arabs call punishment and blessing "days," like His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("And remind them of the days of God"). Everything that has passed over you of good or evil is "days."

﴿قُلْ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ﴾ ("Say: Wait, I am with you among those who wait").

﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("Then We save Our messengers and those who believed") with them when the punishment descends. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ ("Thus") — as We saved them.

﴿كَذلِكَ حَقًّا﴾ ("Thus, as a truth") — obligatory — ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ ("upon Us"), without doubt, ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("We save the believers") through you, O Muhammad. Yaʿqūb read ﴿نُنْجِ رُسُلَنا﴾ with lightening (the single nūn), and al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ with lightening, while the others doubled them. They are two eloquent dialects: anjā yunjī injāʾan and najjā yunajjī tanjiyatan have the same meaning.

Say: "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, which I invite you to, [then know that] I do not worship those whom you worship besides God, the idols which neither understand, nor act, nor see, nor hear, nor harm, nor benefit. Rather, I worship God, who causes you to die." (The phrase means: who causes them to submit and takes their souls.)

"And I have been commanded to be among the believers, and to set your face [towards the religion]." Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] your deed. It was also said: [it means] yourself, i.e., remain upright in the religion, ḥanīfan (inclining sincerely to the truth), "and do not be among the polytheists."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said from the pulpit: "I have not worshipped my Lord through monasticism, and the best of religion is the easy ḥanīfiyyah." [88] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/47, no. 5422, with variation.]]

"And do not call upon, besides God, that which neither benefits you if you obey it, nor harms you if you disobey it. If you do so and worship other than God, then you are indeed, at that point, among the wrongdoers," those who harm themselves, placing worship in other than its proper place. "And if God touches you with harm," i.e., afflicts you with trial and hardship, "there is none to remove it except Him. And if He wills good for you," i.e., ease and blessing, "there is none to repel His bounty," meaning none to withhold His provision.

"He bestows it upon whom He wills of His servants, from among them, [whether harm or good]," and "He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful."

"Say: O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord," meaning the Qur'an, in which there is clarification.

"Whoever is guided, it is only for his own soul" [i.e., he has the reward of his guidance], "and whoever goes astray, it is only against it," i.e., upon himself is the burden. "And I am not over you a guardian," meaning a guarantor and a watcher who preserves your deeds. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

"And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until God judges," i.e., [judges concerning] your victory, the subduing of your enemies, and the manifestation of His religion. "And He is the best of judges."

al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered the Ansar, and the best of them had assembled, and he said:

"Indeed, after me you will find preference given to others, so be patient until you meet me." [89] Anas said: "We did not remain patient." He had commanded them to be patient, as God had commanded him.

'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib said: When Mu'awiyah came to Madinah, the Ansar went out to greet him, but Abu Qatadah stayed behind. Then he entered upon him later, and [Mu'awiyah] said: "What is wrong with you that you did not greet us?" He said: "We had no mounts." He said: "Then where are the water-camels?" He said: "We tied them up in pursuit of you and your father on the day of Badr." And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said: "Be patient until you meet me." [90] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/38.]] They said: "Then we shall be patient." Concerning this, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hassan ibn Thabit said:

Unquestionably, inform Mu'awiyah ibn Harb... Commander of the Believers, my words [[Variant: "nabaʾ" (news); another variant: "ʿannī kalāmī" (my speech).]] are a speech:

"Indeed we shall be patient, and we shall await you... until the Day of Mutual Loss and Dispute."
[[Al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 11/61, no. 19909; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 8/389.]]

al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered the Ansar, and the best of them had assembled, and he said:

"Indeed, after me you will find preference given to others, so be patient until you meet me." [89] Anas said: "We did not remain patient." He had commanded them to be patient, as God had commanded him.

'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib said: When Mu'awiyah came to Madinah, the Ansar went out to greet him, but Abu Qatadah stayed behind. Then he entered upon him later, and [Mu'awiyah] said: "What is wrong with you that you did not greet us?" He said: "We had no mounts." He said: "Then where are the water-camels?" He said: "We tied them up in pursuit of you and your father on the day of Badr." And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said: "Be patient until you meet me." [90] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/38.]] They said: "Then we shall be patient." Concerning this, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hassan ibn Thabit said:

Unquestionably, inform Mu'awiyah ibn Harb... Commander of the Believers, my words [[Variant: "nabaʾ" (news); another variant: "ʿannī kalāmī" (my speech).]] are a speech:

"Indeed we shall be patient, and we shall await you... until the Day of Mutual Loss and Dispute."
